The nonconvex instances covered by our bounds therefore have their negative curvature in directions that involve active bounds or integer coordinates.' verifier.reasoning:
The core claim holds. In intro.tex 138-145, the paragraph opens "Growth restricts where nonconvexity can occur" and then says "The nonconvex instances covered by our bounds therefore have their negative curvature in directions that involve active bounds or integer coordinates". Remark 3.4 (setting-growthcert.tex 63-65) repeats the second sentence, and CONVENTIONS §5 prescribes it.

That conclusion follows from minimality alone. Lemma 3.3(b), first sentence, says that at any minimizer zeta_{J0}=0 and H_{J0J0} ⪰ 0, which is the second-order necessary condition. So every box QP has the property at every minimizer, with or without growth. The point is even sharper than the reviewer says. For box QPs, point growth with some g>0 is equivalent to having a unique minimizer: Definition 3.2(a) gives one direction, and Lemma 6.12 (exact.tex 300) gives the other. Qualitatively, then, growth adds only uniqueness. What actually restricts the instances is the size of the constants.

Nothing elsewhere in the paper corrects this framing. I searched intro, setting, growth, limits, conclusion and abstract.

Exact check: process/w4/checks/verify-C-writing-3.py (sympy).
- F=-(x1-1/2)^2 on [0,1]^2 has no unique minimizer, so it has no point growth. Yet at the minimizer (0,1/2), H_{J0J0}=[0] ⪰ 0 and the only negative curvature is along the active coordinate x1.
- Example 5.12: J0={rho}, H_{J0J0}=2=2g with g=1/2, and the block Hessian is indefinite.

The reviewer overstates two things:
1. It says the restrictions growth adds "are not stated". The local one is stated, in the same intro paragraph and in Remark 3.4: point growth makes the block positive definite, and weighted growth gives H_{J0J0} ⪰ 2γ diag(L_i). Only the quantitative point-growth form (2gI, and hence κ ≥ 2L/λ_min) is missing. The global restriction is the definition of growth itself, which the intro gives at lines 43-46. Its consequence for other local minima is spelled out in setting.tex 124-130, but not in the intro.
2. Its proposed sentence "nearly tied local minima far apart force a large condition number" is false when L=0. Example: F=-(x-1/2)^2+εx on [0,1]. The minima at 0 and 1 are tied within ε and lie at distance 1. The largest growth constant is g=ε, but L=max{H11,0}=0, so κ=1 (checked exactly). The correct statement is the inequality κ ≥ L||x'-x*||^2/(F(x')-OPT).

The reviewer's other claims are correct:
- κ ≥ L/g ≥ 2L/λ_min(H_{J0J0}) when J0 is nonempty.
- An instance whose minimizer is interior to an all-continuous box has point growth only if F is strongly convex (Lemma 3.3(b), last sentence).

Severity: no theorem or stated fact is false, and the growth-specific local bound is already in the paragraph. The defect is a misattributed framing sentence and a "therefore" that rests on minimality, not on growth. In a scope paragraph about the central hypothesis an expert will notice it, so it should be fixed. It is a minor issue, not a major one.

intro.tex: replace lines 138-145, from "Growth restricts" through "(Example~\ref{ex:family}).", with the text below. Keep "The condition number can be large: ..." and the rest of the paragraph.

For a box QP, minimality alone confines nonconvexity: at every minimizer, the
Hessian block $H_{J_0J_0}$ of the continuous coordinates strictly inside their
bounds is positive semidefinite, so every direction of negative curvature
involves active bounds or integer coordinates. Growth adds quantitative
conditions (Lemma~\ref{lem:growthcert}). Locally, point growth forces
$H_{J_0J_0}\succeq2gI$, so $\kappa\ge2L/\lambda_{\min}(H_{J_0J_0})$ if
$J_0\ne\emptyset$, and weighted growth forces
$H_{J_0J_0}\succeq2\gamma\diag(L_i)_{i\in J_0}$. Globally, every other local
minimizer $x'$ satisfies $F(x')-\OPT\ge g\norm{x'-x^*}^2$, so
$\kappa\ge L\norm{x'-x^*}^2/(F(x')-\OPT)$. Within these conditions an
instance can have indefinite Hessian blocks, $\kappa\le\frac{21}4$ and
exponentially many strict local minima (Example~\ref{ex:family}).

setting-growthcert.tex, Remark 3.4: replace lines 60-66, through "(Example~\ref{ex:family}).", with the text below. Keep lines 67-69 ("Part~(a) certifies growth ...").

For a box QP, the block $H_{J_0J_0}$ at a minimizer is positive semidefinite
(Lemma~\ref{lem:growthcert}(b)), so at every minimizer, with or without growth,
every direction of negative curvature involves active bounds or integer
coordinates. For box QPs, point growth with some $g>0$ is equivalent to
uniqueness of the minimizer (Lemma~\ref{lem:unique-growth}); what restricts
the instances is the size of the constants. Point growth gives
$H_{J_0J_0}\succeq2gI$, hence $\kappa\ge2L/\lambda_{\min}(H_{J_0J_0})$ if
$J_0\ne\emptyset$, and weighted growth gives
$H_{J_0J_0}\succeq2\gamma\diag(L_i)_{i\in J_0}$. For every $x'\in X$ with
$F(x')>\OPT$, \eqref{eq:growth} gives $\kappa\ge L\norm{x'-x^*}^2/(F(x')-\OPT)$
and \eqref{eq:wgrowth} gives
$\bar\kappa\ge\norm{x'-x^*}_{\mathbf L}^2/(F(x')-\OPT)$. Within these
conditions an instance can have indefinite Hessian blocks,
$\kappa\le\frac{21}4$ and exponentially many strict local minima
(Example~\ref{ex:family}).

CONVENTIONS §5: replace the "Growth scope" bullet with the following. Minimality alone gives H_{J0J0} ⪰ 0 at every minimizer of a box QP, so negative curvature always involves active bounds or integer coordinates; never attribute this to growth. Growth adds H_{J0J0} ⪰ 2gI under point growth (so κ ≥ 2L/λ_min(H_{J0J0}) if J0 ≠ ∅) and H_{J0J0} ⪰ 2γ diag(L_i) under weighted growth. Globally, κ ≥ L||x'-x*||^2/(F(x')-OPT) for every other local minimizer x'. Do not write "nearly tied minima force a large κ" without this inequality: with L=0, κ=1 for every g. Cite Example ex:family for indefinite blocks, κ ≤ 21/4 and exponentially many strict local minima.

If the C-writing-4 abstract mentions the scope caveat, apply the same correction there.
